import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from datetime import datetime

# Data
data = {
    'ID': [5524, 2174, 4141, 6182, 5324],
    'Year_Birth': [1957, 1954, 1965, 1984, 1981],
    'Education': ['Graduation', 'Graduation', 'Graduation', 'Graduation', 'PhD'],
    'Marital_Status': ['Single', 'Single', 'Together', 'Together', 'Married'],
    'Income': [58138.0, 46344.0, 71613.0, 26646.0, 58293.0],
    'Kidhome': [0, 1, 0, 1, 1],
    'Teenhome': [0, 1, 0, 0, 0],
    'Dt_Customer': ['04-09-2012', '08-03-2014', '21-08-2013', '10-02-2014', '19-01-2014'],
    'Recency': [58, 38, 26, 26, 94],
    'MntWines': [635, 11, 426, 11, 173],
    'MntFruits': [88, 1, 49, 4, 43],
    'MntMeatProducts': [546, 6, 127, 20, 118],
    'MntFishProducts': [172, 2, 111, 10, 46],
    'MntSweetProducts': [88, 1, 21, 3, 27],
    'MntGoldProds': [88, 6, 42, 5, 15],
    'NumDealsPurchases': [3, 2, 1, 2, 5],
    'NumWebPurchases': [8, 1, 8, 2, 5],
    'NumCatalogPurchases': [10, 1, 2, 0, 3],
    'NumStorePurchases': [4, 2, 10, 4, 6],
    'NumWebVisitsMonth': [7, 5, 4, 6, 5],
    'AcceptedCmp3': [0, 0, 0, 0, 0],
    'AcceptedCmp4': [0, 0, 0, 0, 0],
    'AcceptedCmp5': [0, 0, 0, 0, 0],
    'AcceptedCmp1': [0, 0, 0, 0, 0],
    'AcceptedCmp2': [0, 0, 0, 0, 0],
    'Complain': [0, 0, 0, 0, 0],
    'Z_CostContact': [3, 3, 3, 3, 3],
    'Z_Revenue': [11, 11, 11, 11, 11],
    'Response': [1, 0, 0, 0, 0]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Convert date column
df['Dt_Customer'] = pd.to_datetime(df['Dt_Customer'], format='%d-%m-%Y')
df['Age'] = datetime.now().year - df['Year_Birth']

# Set style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(18, 12))

# 1. Income distribution by marital status
plt.subplot(2, 3, 1)
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='Marital_Status', y='Income', palette='Set2')
plt.title('Income Distribution by Marital Status')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

# 2. Spending categories comparison
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 
                 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
spending_data = df[spending_cols].mean()
plt.subplot(2, 3, 2)
spending_data.plot(kind='bar', color=sns.color_palette('husl', len(spending_cols)))
plt.title('Average Spending by Category')
plt.ylabel('Amount Spent')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

# 3. Purchase channels comparison
purchase_cols = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases']
purchase_data = df[purchase_cols].mean()
plt.subplot(2, 3, 3)
purchase_data.plot(kind='bar', color=sns.color_palette('Set3', len(purchase_cols)))
plt.title('Average Purchases by Channel')
plt.ylabel('Number of Purchases')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

# 4. Age vs Income scatter plot
plt.subplot(2, 3, 4)
scatter = plt.scatter(df['Age'], df['Income'], c=df['Response'], 
                      cmap='coolwarm', s=100, alpha=0.7, edgecolors='black')
plt.xlabel('Age')
plt.ylabel('Income')
plt.title('Age vs Income (colored by Campaign Response)')
plt.colorbar(scatter, label='Campaign Response')

# 5. Household composition
plt.subplot(2, 3, 5)
household_data = df[['Kidhome', 'Teenhome']].sum()
household_data.plot(kind='pie', autopct='%1.1f%%', colors=['lightblue', 'lightcoral'])
plt.title('Household Composition')
plt.ylabel('')

# 6. Recency distribution
plt.subplot(2, 3, 6)
sns.histplot(df['Recency'], bins=10, kde=True, color='purple')
plt.title('Recency Distribution (Days since last purchase)')
plt.xlabel('Recency (days)')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
